text:
Deadlines are a part of professional life, but they don’t have to be a source of constant stress. The key is effective time management. Start by breaking a large project into smaller, manageable tasks and estimating how long each will take. This brings clarity and prevents last-minute panic.

Prioritization is equally important. Not all tasks carry the same weight, so focus on what is most critical to the project’s success first. At the same time, practice scope management: be realistic about what you can achieve and don’t be afraid to say no to extra requests. Finally, maintain open communication with your team or client. If a deadline is at risk, speak up early and propose a new timeline—it’s always better than surprising anyone at the end.
